title: Unicode Multibyte Expansion in the Chronos Interpreter: Formal Analysis of Emoji-Induced Memory Inflation
topic: Why a Single Emoji Quadruples Aether-Interpreter String Memory
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: The Chronos interpreter stores strings as immutable UTF-8 byte sequences, a design that directly couples memory consumption to the multibyte representation of Unicode code points. This work investigates how a single emoji, encoded in four UTF-8 bytes, inflates the interpreter's string memory by a factor of four relative to an ASCII character. We formalize the memory model, prove that appending a character increases memory by the exact byte count of the character, and analyze the asymptotic complexity of the underlying balanced search structure used for string interning. Theoretical bounds confirm that search and insertion remain $O(\log N)$, while the memory footprint grows linearly with the total byte count. No empirical wall-clock measurements are reported; all results are derived from static analysis and formal proofs. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Chronos-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261102_030127_why_a_single_emoji_quadruples}
